edges.effect_quant: Prospective cohort data suggest a small average effect that is directionally consistent but not dramatic.
edges.mechanism: This factor changes substrate delivery, microbial competition, short-chain fatty-acid production, or early-life colonization patterns in the gut. Those changes are most directly linked to Colorectal cancer when the endpoint is microbial composition, barrier function, or a gut-mediated immune phenotype.
edges.summary: Prospective cohort data link soluble fiber to lower risk of colorectal cancer in general adult. The average effect is usually small rather than dramatic, so this edge is better read as a risk modifier than a stand-alone cause or cure.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.

evidence.citation: ShenY et al 2024 BMC Public Health
